question.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ ${S}_{yy}$ is the sum of the squared deviations of the data ${y}_{i}$ from the mean $\overset{―}{y},$ that is

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{yy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we calculate the sample mean $\overset{―}{y}:$

$$
\overset{―}{y}=\frac{16+14+23+17+15}{5}=17.
$$

Next, we calculate the differences between the ${y}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}$, and their squares.

| **$\,{x}_{i}\,$** | $5$ | $11$ | $9$ | $12$ | $18$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **$\,{y}_{i}\,$** | $16$ | $14$ | $23$ | $17$ | $15$ |
| **$\,({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})\,$** | $-1$ | $-3$ | $6$ | $0$ | $-2$ |
| **$\,({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2}\,$** | $1$ | $9$ | $36$ | $0$ | $4$ |

Therefore, ${S}_{yy}$ is

$$
{S}_{yy}=1+9+36+0+4=50.
$$
